skill.name: incremental-implementation
skill.description: Guides multi-file changes through small, complete implementation slices. Each slice is tested, verified, committed, and kept easy to reverse.
skill.summary: Implement complex changes through focused, verifiable, and reversible slices.
skill.author: addyosmani

content.value_statement: Large changes become difficult to test, review, and reverse. This skill divides implementation into focused slices with verification, commits, flags, and final checks.
actual_capabilities: Divides multi-file features into small, complete vertical slices.
Selects vertical, contract-first, or risk-first slicing strategies.
Requires relevant tests, builds, type checks, and lint checks after changes.
Keeps each increment focused, compilable, and independently reversible.
Uses disabled-by-default feature flags for incomplete features.
Records out-of-scope improvements without changing unrelated code.
limitations: Does not replace a project-specific plan, test suite, or build process.
Provides little value for an already minimal single-file or single-function change.
Does not supply repository-specific implementation details without project context.
Relies on the repository toolchain and available agent permissions for verification.

use_cases.title: Deliver a Multi-File Feature
use_cases.description: Break a feature into complete paths that remain testable and reviewable after every increment.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Frontend and Backend Work
use_cases.description: Define contracts first, then develop compatible backend and frontend slices before integration.

use_cases.title: Reduce Refactoring Risk
use_cases.description: Sequence focused changes with tests and reversible commits to isolate failures quickly.

prompt_templates.title: Plan the First Slice
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this task and propose the smallest complete first slice. Define scope, excluded work, verification steps, and a completion condition.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a clear starting point for a multi-file task.

prompt_templates.title: Implement One Planned Increment
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement the next approved slice only. Run relevant project checks, report results, and note unrelated issues without changing them.
prompt_templates.scenario: An engineer is continuing work from an existing implementation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Slicing Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare vertical, contract-first, and risk-first approaches for this feature. Recommend one and produce ordered, independently verifiable increments.
prompt_templates.scenario: A technical lead must structure work across components or teams.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Controlled Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an incremental rollout plan for this high-risk change. Include safe defaults, feature flags, migrations, rollback steps, verification gates, and commit boundaries.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user is preparing a risky production change.

output_examples.input: Add task creation, listing, editing, and deletion across the database, API, and interface.
output: Slice 1: Add task creation across all layers and verify the complete path.
Slice 2: Add task listing and confirm existing creation behavior remains stable.
Slice 3: Add editing with focused tests and an independent commit.
Slice 4: Add deletion with confirmation, tests, and final end-to-end verification.

output_examples.input: Prepare an unfinished sharing feature for gradual integration.
output_examples.output: Introduce a disabled-by-default feature flag, deliver one complete sharing path, verify both flag states, and keep each increment reversible.

output_examples.input: Refactor a risky data path while preserving current behavior.
output: Prove the uncertain dependency first with a focused test.
Move one behavior at a time while keeping the build green.
Run project-wide verification after all local increments pass.

best_practices: Define one observable outcome and explicit exclusions for every increment.
Run relevant verification after each meaningful change and record the result.
Keep commits focused so each increment can be reviewed or reverted independently.
anti_patterns: Do not combine feature work, unrelated cleanup, and broad refactoring in one increment.
Do not defer all testing until the complete feature is implemented.
Do not expose unfinished behavior without a disabled-by-default control.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for multi-file features, refactors, migrations, or any change that benefits from several verified steps.

faq.question: When is this skill unnecessary?
faq.answer: Skip it when a single-file, single-function change is already minimal and easy to verify.

faq.question: What is a vertical slice?
faq.answer: A vertical slice delivers one complete user-visible path across every required system layer.

faq.question: How should incomplete features be merged?
faq.answer: Use a disabled-by-default feature flag and verify behavior with the flag both enabled and disabled.

faq.question: Should every slice have a separate commit?
faq.answer: Yes. Focused commits improve review, diagnosis, and rollback when each slice represents one logical change.

faq.question: Does this skill choose project commands?
faq.answer: No. It uses the repository test, build, type-checking, and lint commands that the project already defines.
